h1: The 6 Best Printers for Black and White Documents, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Black and White Printers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 printers for black and white documents, from mono lasers to color lasers and inkjets, compared on toner, duplex and speed.
mainKeyword: printer for black and white documents
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the printer to buy if 90 percent of your pages are black and white text, with a mono laser engine, duplex printing and a toner-save mode. The HP LaserJet M209d is the cheaper wired option, the Brother HL-L3220CDW and Canon MF753Cdw II add color when you need it, and the inkjets are for people who mix documents with grayscale graphics.
intro: Most people who print black and white pages are paying for color they never use. A color inkjet keeps four ink channels alive even when you print only text, and any idle spell leaves cartridges drying and clogging. A monochrome laser has none of that: one toner, no nozzles, and pages that stay sharp. Choosing a printer for plain documents is mostly about picking the right engine and then matching speed and connectivity.

We reviewed eight printers from their listings and spec sheets, kept six, and ranked them for black and white document work. We set aside two photo-oriented inkjets that serve a different buyer. The ranking looks at print engine, duplex printing, speed, connectivity, toner handling and warranty. Price buckets replace exact prices, and where a listing leaves out a figure, we say so.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A compact mono laser with duplex, wireless and mobile printing and a toner-save mode.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a compact monochrome laser with automatic duplex printing, wireless and mobile printing, and a toner-save mode. Because it uses toner, there is no risk of cartridges drying out while it sits idle. It falls in the $200 to $500 range.

For documents, this is the benchmark. Laser output is crisp and resistant to smearing, which matters for contracts, reports and forms. The toner-save mode stretches a cartridge for drafts and internal copies, and duplex printing halves paper use. Because it is an all-in-one, it also scans and copies. The price is higher than a plain printer, and it prints in black and white only.

Buy it if almost everything you print is text. Skip it if you occasionally need color.
cons: Costs more than a plain printer
products.idealFor: Households where nearly all printing is text.

products.name: HP LaserJet M209d Laser Printer, Black and White
products.verdict: A compact USB-only mono laser with automatic duplex printing for around $100 to $200.
products.description:
The M209d is a monochrome laser with automatic duplex printing and a wired USB connection only. It has a compact home office design and no risk of idle toner drying. It sits in the $100 to $200 range.

The lack of wireless is the whole story. There is no network to join, no router password and no printer-offline error on a laptop. You plug in a cable and print. That makes it the simplest and cheapest way to get a real laser on a desk. The cost of that simplicity is flexibility: only the computer connected by cable can print, and phones cannot, and there is no scanner or copier.

Buy it if one computer prints all the text. Skip it if you want to print from a phone or share between several people.
products.idealFor: A single-computer desk that prints text.
products.skipIf: You print from phones or share the printer.

products.name: Brother HL-L3220CDW Wireless Color Laser Printer
products.verdict: A color laser that handles black and white text at 19 ppm, with a 250-sheet tray and duplex.
products.description:
The HL-L3220CDW is a wireless color laser that works well in black and white mode, with a 19 page-per-minute print speed, a 250-sheet paper tray, duplex printing and mobile compatibility. It falls in the $200 to $500 range.

It earns third place because it gives you the occasional color page at laser prices without forcing you onto an inkjet. A color laser uses four toners, so the replacement set costs more than a single black cartridge, but toner lasts long. At 19 ppm it is not a fast printer, and for pure text the Brother mono model is cheaper to run.

Buy it if most of your printing is black and white but you need a color page now and then. Skip it if you will never print color.
cons: Four toners cost more than one
products.idealFor: Mostly-B&W users who need color occasionally.

products.name: Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II Wireless Duplex Laser Printer
products.verdict: A color laser all-in-one with a 35 ppm print speed, a document feeder and a 3-year warranty.
products.description:
The MF753Cdw II is a color laser all-in-one that prints in black and white as well, with a 35 page-per-minute speed, an automatic document feeder, duplex printing and a 3-year limited warranty. It sits in the $200 to $500 range.

The speed and warranty are what set it apart. At 35 ppm it is far quicker than the Brother color model, which matters when you print a long report. A three-year warranty is generous for a printer. It ranks fourth because it is an office-class machine with a larger body, and because color toner is costly to replace.

Buy it if you print a lot, scan stacks and want a long warranty. Skip it if you have a small desk.
cons: Color toner is costly to replace
products.idealFor: Busy offices that print and scan a lot.

products.name: Brother INKvestment MCF-J5010DW Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: A wireless color inkjet with INKvestment high-capacity cartridges, 2-sided copy and scan and a 2.7 inch touchscreen.
products.description:
The MFC-J5010DW uses Brother's INKvestment high-capacity cartridges, scans and copies on both sides automatically, and has a 2.7 inch color touchscreen. It is a wireless color inkjet, not a laser, in the $200 to $500 range.

It makes sense here if you mix black and white documents with grayscale graphics and photos, and want fewer cartridge swaps. High-capacity cartridges reduce how often you replace ink, which matters for a busier office. It ranks fifth because an inkjet still cannot match laser sharpness on text or avoid the risk of clogged nozzles after long idle periods.

Buy it if you need graphics and text in one printer and want fewer ink changes. Skip it if you only print text.
cons: Inkjet text is less crisp than laser
Cartridges can dry after idle spells
products.idealFor: Mixed text and graphics at moderate volume.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 9135 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A color inkjet with an automatic document feeder, duplex print and scan and a 3-month Instant Ink trial.
products.description:
The OfficeJet Pro 9135 is a color inkjet with an automatic document feeder, duplex printing and scanning, and a 3-month Instant Ink trial. It is rated for office use and sits in the $200 to $500 range.

It appears last because black and white text is a job inkjets do adequately but not best. The feeder, duplex scanning and office rating make it a versatile machine, and the ink trial can lower early costs. Still, a user with only text pages is paying for color capability and ink maintenance that a mono laser avoids.

Buy it if you mix text with grayscale pictures and charts and want a feeder. Skip it if documents are your only use.
cons: Inkjet is not ideal for pure text
products.idealFor: Mixed documents with charts and pictures.
products.skipIf: You print only black and white text.

methodology.title: Print engine
methodology.description: We compared monochrome lasers, color lasers in black and white mode and color inkjets, since the engine decides sharpness and upkeep.

methodology.title: Toner and ink handling
methodology.description: Toner-save modes, high-capacity cartridges and the risk of idle drying were weighed for light and heavy users.

methodology.title: Speed and capacity
methodology.description: Print speeds from 19 to 35 ppm and tray sizes such as 250 sheets were checked against office demand.

methodology.title: Connectivity
methodology.description: Wired USB, wireless and mobile printing were compared, including the one printer that works only over a cable.

methodology.title: Warranty and value
methodology.description: Stated warranties and the $100 to $200 and $200 to $500 brackets were weighed together.

whatMatters.detail: Laser toner is fused onto the page, which gives sharp, smear-resistant text and no dried-ink problems. Inkjets do text acceptably but are better for graphics. For documents, a laser is the more reliable choice.

A toner-save mode lightens output to stretch a cartridge, useful for drafts. Mono lasers usually have the lowest cost per page. A color laser has to replace four toners, so the cost of a full set is higher.

Speed in pages per minute decides how long a long document takes. 19 ppm is adequate for home use, and 35 ppm suits an office. A first-page-out time matters for single sheets, but few listings state it.

A USB-only printer, like the HP M209d, avoids network setup but only serves one computer. Wireless adds convenience and mobile printing but also the chance of an offline error. Pick the connection that matches how many devices will print.
Automatic duplex halves paper use for reports. A 250-sheet tray means less reloading. Look for the words automatic duplex and a tray capacity in the spec list.

cards.text: Duplex printing, a toner-save mode for drafts, wireless setup and a low cost per page. A scanner is handy for forms.

faq.q: Why choose a laser for black and white documents?
faq.a: Toner is a dry powder that does not clog, so a laser prints a page after months of rest. Text is sharp, smear-resistant and cheap per page. Inkjets are better for photos and graphics.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a printer for documents?
faq.a: Paying for color you will not use. A color inkjet costs more in ink maintenance, and cartridges dry out when idle. A monochrome laser fits a text-only workload better.

faq.q: Is the Brother DCP-L2640DW worth it over the HP M209d?
faq.a: If you want wireless printing, mobile printing and scanning, yes. The HP M209d costs less but works only over a USB cable and prints only. Choose by how many devices must print.
Unbox, remove the packing tape, install the toner, load paper and connect. Wireless models need a network setup through the display or app. The HP M209d needs only a cable and a driver.

faq.q: Can a color laser print black and white cheaply?
faq.a: Yes, in black and white mode it uses only the black toner. The cost per page is higher than a mono laser's, and the full toner set costs more to replace, but the quality is similar.

faq.q: Do I need to worry about toner drying out?
faq.a: No. Toner is powder, so an idle laser needs no cleaning cycles. This is the biggest practical advantage over an inkjet for occasional printing.

finalTake: For black and white documents, the Brother DCP-L2640DW wins this ranking on a mono laser engine, duplex, wireless and a toner-save mode. The HP LaserJet M209d is the cheapest laser if you can use a cable, the Brother HL-L3220CDW and Canon MF753Cdw II add color, and the inkjets suit mixed work. Match the engine to your pages, not your ambitions.
